verses.verse:
अंगुलीयक एकस्मिन् कूर्याद् भागचतुष्टयम्।
अंगुष्ठाग्रेण गृहणीयात् तांश्च भागान् क्रमेण वै।९३।
verses.text: On each finger one should make four parts, and take those parts in order with the tip of the thumb.

verses.verse:
ततः परांगुलीयेषु गणयेत् पूर्ववत् क्रमात्।
तेन षोड़श मात्राः स्यूरंगुलीय चतुष्टयें।९४।
verses.text: Then on the other fingers one should count in order as before; thus there will be sixteen mātrās (beats) on the four fingers.

commentary.text: That is, if you count by taking each finger as four parts and placing the tip of the thumb on those parts in order, you can easily count up to 16 mātrās (beats).

Just as any flowing river has four directions, so practice too stays alive in four ways: sunanā, cunanā, gunanā and dhunanā — śravaṇa (listening), cayana (choosing), gunana (pondering) and upayoga (use). If you listen to any song or tune with concentration, then pick out from it a few things that matter to you, then sit alone and hum it, and then keep using it at the right time, any practice will keep blossoming and putting out leaves, and will keep flowing along with life. Now some methods of practising the notes with laya (tempo) are presented.

subsection.title: Practice of the Tongue and of the Fingers
